text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Threats by former combatants from both sides in Namibia's war over independence have withdrawn a threat to carry out suicide bombings after a meeting with government officials.
- Exchange controls have been lifted in Namibia for institutional and corporate investors and individuals will eventually be able to open foreign currency accounts, the Bank of Namibia said.
- Laurent Kabila of the Democratic Republic of the Congo is continuing to campaign for international support for his country's economic reconstruction.

- A new political party is to be formed this week. Founders of the Namibia Movement for Independent Candidates say they want it to bring young people into politics in a group without historical burdens.
- Agriculture Minister Helmuth Angula said organised agriculture will in future only receive 40 percent of the statutory levies collected by the meat producers' board.
- The national planning commission has made available N$3 million to the University of Namibia to develop a regional campus at Oshakati and a research station at Hentiesbay.
